newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia, Macedonia sign pact to liberalise trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatia, Macedonia sign pact to liberalise trade.

text.p: Croatia and Macedonia initialled on Wednesday an agreement on liberalising mutual trade, Croatian news agency reported.
New Croatian Economy Minsiter Nenad Porges said the pact would pave the way for doubling trade between the two former Yugoslav republics to $200 million from $100 million.
The agreeement, initialled by deputy economy ministers in Zagreb, would probably be signed in Macedonia by end-May, Porges said.
Following the agreement, import taxes on industrial and agricultural products will be reduced. Some agricultural products, to be defined through concession deals, would be free of duty.
Croatian deputy Economy Minister Slavko Begic said the pact would immediately raise the export of Croatian pharmaceutical and agricultural products, and oil derivatives to Macedonia.
Croatia is in talks with the World Trade Organisation on becoming a member.
